q18395.en: In an at-grade junction (crossroads), two or more roads cross at the same level.

explain.short: 'A raso' means 'at ground level': the roads meet on the same level, with no bridge.
explain.rule: An at-grade junction (intersezione a raso) is a crossroads where roads meet on the same level, so their traffic flows cross.
explain.trap: 'a raso' does not mean 'small': it means 'at the same level'.

sceneParams.caption: Roads meet on the same level

q18396.en: An at-grade junction (crossroads) can be controlled by traffic lights.

explain.short: Many ordinary crossroads have traffic lights to decide who goes first.
explain.rule: An at-grade junction (intersezione a raso) is a crossroads where roads meet on the same level, so their traffic flows cross.
explain.trap: 'può' means 'can': lights are possible, not compulsory.

sceneParams.caption: A crossroads can have traffic lights

q18397.en: An at-grade junction (crossroads) is an intersection of two or more roads placed at the same level.

explain.short: That is the definition: roads that cross each other on the same level.
explain.rule: An at-grade junction (intersezione a raso) is a crossroads where roads meet on the same level, so their traffic flows cross.
explain.trap: 'poste allo stesso livello' is the key: same level, no bridges.

sceneParams.caption: Two or more roads on the same level

q18398.en: An at-grade junction (crossroads) requires paying attention to vehicles coming from the crossing roads.

explain.short: At a crossroads other cars can come from the side roads, so you must watch them.
explain.rule: An at-grade junction (intersezione a raso) is a crossroads where roads meet on the same level, so their traffic flows cross.
explain.trap: 'richiede' means 'requires': watching is a real duty here.

sceneParams.caption: Watch cars from the other roads

q18399.en: An at-grade junction (crossroads) is a crossing between a state road and tram tracks.

explain.short: An at-grade junction is between ROADS. A road crossing rails is a different thing (a level crossing).
explain.rule: An at-grade junction (intersezione a raso) is a crossroads where roads meet on the same level, so their traffic flows cross.
explain.trap: 'binari del tram' (tram tracks) is the wrong element: junctions join roads.

sceneParams.caption: A junction joins roads, not tram tracks

q18400.en: An at-grade junction (crossroads) is a crossing between a state road and a driveway.

explain.short: A driveway (passo carrabile) is an entrance to private property, not a road. A crossroads joins roads.
explain.rule: An at-grade junction (intersezione a raso) is a crossroads where roads meet on the same level, so their traffic flows cross.
explain.trap: 'passo carrabile' means a driveway, not a road.

sceneParams.caption: A driveway is not a road

q18401.en: An at-grade junction (crossroads) is a level crossing equipped with barriers or half-barriers.

explain.short: A level crossing (passaggio a livello) is road and railway. A crossroads is road and road.
explain.rule: An at-grade junction (intersezione a raso) is a crossroads where roads meet on the same level, so their traffic flows cross.
explain.trap: Both use the word 'livello', but 'passaggio a livello' is about trains.

sceneParams.caption: Level crossing = railway, not a crossroads

q18402.en: An at-grade junction (crossroads) is an intersection on different levels.

explain.short: 'A raso' means the SAME level. 'Livelli sfalsati' means different levels, with bridges: the opposite.
explain.rule: An at-grade junction (intersezione a raso) is a crossroads where roads meet on the same level, so their traffic flows cross.
explain.trap: 'livelli sfalsati' (different levels) is the opposite of 'a raso'.

sceneParams.caption: A raso = same level, not different levels

q18403.en: An at-grade junction (crossroads) is a set of overpasses, underpasses and ramps.

explain.short: Overpasses, underpasses and ramps belong to a junction on different levels, not to one at the same level.
explain.rule: An at-grade junction (intersezione a raso) is a crossroads where roads meet on the same level, so their traffic flows cross.
explain.trap: 'sovrappassi, sottopassi' describe bridges and tunnels: not 'a raso'.

sceneParams.caption: No bridges or ramps: roads meet on one level

q18404.en: A limited traffic zone is an area where vehicle traffic can be limited only at certain hours.

explain.short: Many ZTLs are closed only at some times of day, for example during the day in the town centre.
explain.rule: A ZTL (zona a traffico limitato) is a zone where traffic is limited by hours, vehicle type or user type; only authorised vehicles enter.
explain.trap: Here 'solo' (only) is correct: the limit can apply to some hours only.

sceneParams.caption: A ZTL can be limited only at some hours
lines: Traffic limited in a marked zone
Start and end signs mark it

q18405.en: A limited traffic zone is an area in which traffic can be limited only for particular categories of vehicles.

explain.short: The town can close a ZTL only to some kinds of vehicles, for example trucks or polluting cars.
explain.rule: A ZTL (zona a traffico limitato) is a zone where traffic is limited by hours, vehicle type or user type; only authorised vehicles enter.
explain.trap: 'solo di particolari categorie' is right: the limit can hit only some vehicles.

sceneParams.caption: The limit can apply to some vehicle types
lines: Traffic limited in a marked zone
Start and end signs mark it

q18406.en: In a limited traffic zone only authorised vehicles may circulate.

explain.short: When the limit is on, only vehicles with permission (residents, taxis, services...) may enter.
explain.rule: A ZTL (zona a traffico limitato) is a zone where traffic is limited by hours, vehicle type or user type; only authorised vehicles enter.
explain.trap: 'autorizzati' (authorised) is the key word: permission is needed.

sceneParams.caption: Only authorised vehicles enter
lines: Traffic limited in a marked zone
Start and end signs mark it

q18407.en: A limited traffic zone is an area in which traffic can be limited only to particular categories of users.

explain.short: Access can be kept for some users only, for example residents or delivery drivers.
explain.rule: A ZTL (zona a traffico limitato) is a zone where traffic is limited by hours, vehicle type or user type; only authorised vehicles enter.
explain.trap: 'utenti' means road users (people), and the limit can depend on them.

sceneParams.caption: Access can be for some users only
lines: Traffic limited in a marked zone
Start and end signs mark it

q18408.en: A limited traffic zone is marked by special start and end road signs.

explain.short: Signs at the entrance and the exit tell you where the ZTL starts and ends, and its hours.
explain.rule: A ZTL (zona a traffico limitato) is a zone where traffic is limited by hours, vehicle type or user type; only authorised vehicles enter.
explain.trap: 'delimitata' means 'bounded / marked out'.

sceneParams.caption: Signs mark the start and end of a ZTL
lines: Traffic limited in a marked zone
Start and end signs mark it

q18409.en: In a limited traffic zone no more than a certain number of vehicles may enter.

explain.short: A ZTL limits by hours, vehicle type or user type, not by counting cars.
explain.rule: A ZTL (zona a traffico limitato) is a zone where traffic is limited by hours, vehicle type or user type; only authorised vehicles enter.
explain.trap: 'un certo numero' (a certain number) is invented: there is no quota.

sceneParams.caption: No car quota: limits by hours, vehicle, user
lines: Traffic limited in a marked zone
Start and end signs mark it

q18410.en: A limited traffic zone is an area where only mopeds and bicycles may pass.

explain.short: A ZTL lets in authorised vehicles of many kinds, not only mopeds and bicycles.
explain.rule: A ZTL (zona a traffico limitato) is a zone where traffic is limited by hours, vehicle type or user type; only authorised vehicles enter.
explain.trap: 'solo... ciclomotori e biciclette' is too narrow and invented.

sceneParams.caption: Not only mopeds and bikes: authorised vehicles
lines: Traffic limited in a marked zone
Start and end signs mark it

q18411.en: A limited traffic zone is an area always closed to motor vehicles.

explain.short: Traffic is LIMITED, not banned: authorised motor vehicles may enter, and often only some hours are closed.
explain.rule: A ZTL (zona a traffico limitato) is a zone where traffic is limited by hours, vehicle type or user type; only authorised vehicles enter.
explain.trap: 'sempre' (always) is the trap: a ZTL limits, it does not always ban.

sceneParams.caption: Limited, not always banned
lines: Traffic limited in a marked zone
Start and end signs mark it

q18412.en: A limited traffic zone is an area closed to pedestrians during the night.

explain.short: A ZTL limits vehicles. Pedestrians can always walk there, day and night.
explain.rule: A ZTL (zona a traffico limitato) is a zone where traffic is limited by hours, vehicle type or user type; only authorised vehicles enter.
explain.trap: 'pedoni' is the trap: the ZTL is about vehicles, not people on foot.

sceneParams.caption: ZTL limits vehicles, not pedestrians
lines: Traffic limited in a marked zone
Start and end signs mark it

q18413.en: At a level crossing you can find barriers.

explain.short: Many level crossings have full barriers that close the road when a train comes.
explain.rule: A level crossing (passaggio a livello) is where road and railway cross on the same level, protected by barriers, red lights or the St Andrew's cross.
explain.trap: 'si possono trovare' means 'may be there', not always.

sceneParams.caption: Barriers close the road for trains
lines: Road and rails cross on one level

q18414.en: At a level crossing you can find half-barriers.

explain.short: Some level crossings have half-barriers, which close only half of the road on each side.
explain.rule: A level crossing (passaggio a livello) is where road and railway cross on the same level, protected by barriers, red lights or the St Andrew's cross.
explain.trap: 'semibarriere' are half-barriers: still a real level crossing device.

sceneParams.caption: Half-barriers are possible too
lines: Road and rails cross on one level

q18415.en: At a level crossing you can find red lights.

explain.short: Red flashing lights warn that a train is coming: you must stop.
explain.rule: A level crossing (passaggio a livello) is where road and railway cross on the same level, protected by barriers, red lights or the St Andrew's cross.
explain.trap: 'rosse' (red) is right; quiz versions with yellow lights are false.

sceneParams.caption: Red lights: a train is coming, stop
lines: Road and rails cross on one level

q18416.en: Near a level crossing there are distance boards.

explain.short: Before a level crossing, boards with red stripes count down the distance to it.
explain.rule: A level crossing (passaggio a livello) is where road and railway cross on the same level, protected by barriers, red lights or the St Andrew's cross.
explain.trap: 'distanziometrici' means 'showing the distance'.

sceneParams.caption: Distance boards before the crossing
lines: Road and rails cross on one level

q18417.en: At a level crossing you can find the St Andrew's cross.

explain.short: The St Andrew's cross (an X-shaped sign) marks a level crossing, often one without barriers.
explain.rule: A level crossing (passaggio a livello) is where road and railway cross on the same level, protected by barriers, red lights or the St Andrew's cross.
explain.trap: 'croce di S. Andrea' is the X-shaped sign: it belongs here.

sceneParams.caption: The X sign marks the railway crossing
lines: Road and rails cross on one level

q18418.en: At a level crossing you can find an acoustic warning device.

explain.short: Many level crossings ring a bell or sound when a train is coming.
explain.rule: A level crossing (passaggio a livello) is where road and railway cross on the same level, protected by barriers, red lights or the St Andrew's cross.
explain.trap: 'acustica' means 'by sound': a bell or buzzer.

sceneParams.caption: A bell can sound when a train comes
lines: Road and rails cross on one level

q18419.en: A level crossing is a railway or tramway overpass.

explain.short: At a level crossing road and rails meet on the SAME level. An overpass is a bridge.
explain.rule: A level crossing (passaggio a livello) is where road and railway cross on the same level, protected by barriers, red lights or the St Andrew's cross.
explain.trap: 'cavalcavia' (overpass, bridge) is the opposite of 'a livello'.

sceneParams.caption: Same level, not a bridge
lines: Road and rails cross on one level

q18420.en: At a level crossing you can find flashing yellow lights.

explain.short: The lights at a level crossing are RED, not yellow.
explain.rule: A level crossing (passaggio a livello) is where road and railway cross on the same level, protected by barriers, red lights or the St Andrew's cross.
explain.trap: 'gialle' (yellow) is the wrong colour: they are red.

sceneParams.caption: Level crossing lights are red, not yellow
lines: Road and rails cross on one level

q18421.en: A level crossing is characterised by a motorway crossing.

explain.short: A level crossing is about road and railway. Motorways never have level crossings.
explain.rule: A level crossing (passaggio a livello) is where road and railway cross on the same level, protected by barriers, red lights or the St Andrew's cross.
explain.trap: 'autostradale' (motorway) is the wrong element: it is about rails.

sceneParams.caption: Road and railway, not a motorway
lines: Road and rails cross on one level

q18422.en: At a level crossing you can find acceleration lanes.

explain.short: Acceleration lanes are for joining a motorway, not for level crossings.
explain.rule: A level crossing (passaggio a livello) is where road and railway cross on the same level, protected by barriers, red lights or the St Andrew's cross.
explain.trap: 'corsie di accelerazione' belong to motorways.

sceneParams.caption: Acceleration lanes are on motorways
lines: Road and rails cross on one level

q18423.en: A level crossing is a driveway.

explain.short: A driveway is an entrance to private property. A level crossing is where road meets railway.
explain.rule: A level crossing (passaggio a livello) is where road and railway cross on the same level, protected by barriers, red lights or the St Andrew's cross.
explain.trap: 'passo carrabile' (driveway) sounds similar to 'passaggio' but is different.

sceneParams.caption: Level crossing = rails, not a driveway
lines: Road and rails cross on one level

q18424.en: A level crossing is characterised by an underpass.

explain.short: An underpass goes UNDER the rails. A level crossing is on the same level.
explain.rule: A level crossing (passaggio a livello) is where road and railway cross on the same level, protected by barriers, red lights or the St Andrew's cross.
explain.trap: 'sottopassaggio' (underpass) is the opposite of 'a livello'.

sceneParams.caption: Same level, no underpass
lines: Road and rails cross on one level

q18425.en: In pedestrian areas zero-emission (electric) vehicles may pass, if expressly allowed.

explain.short: The town may allow electric vehicles into a pedestrian area, but only if a sign says so.
explain.rule: A pedestrian area (area pedonale) is for pedestrians and bicycles; vehicles enter only as listed exceptions (emergency, disabled, allowed e-vehicles).
explain.trap: 'se espressamente consentito' (if expressly allowed) is the condition that makes it right.

sceneParams.caption: Electric vehicles: only if allowed
lines: Emergency with siren + blue light: yes

q18426.en: In pedestrian areas pedestrians may pass.

explain.short: Pedestrian areas are made for people on foot.
explain.rule: A pedestrian area (area pedonale) is for pedestrians and bicycles; vehicles enter only as listed exceptions (emergency, disabled, allowed e-vehicles).
explain.trap: No trap: 'pedoni' are exactly who the area is for.

sceneParams.caption: Pedestrian areas are for pedestrians
lines: Emergency with siren + blue light: yes

q18427.en: In pedestrian areas bicycles may pass.

explain.short: Bicycles are allowed in pedestrian areas (unless a sign says otherwise); ride carefully among people.
explain.rule: A pedestrian area (area pedonale) is for pedestrians and bicycles; vehicles enter only as listed exceptions (emergency, disabled, allowed e-vehicles).
explain.trap: 'biciclette' are allowed, unlike mopeds ('ciclomotori').

sceneParams.caption: Bicycles may enter, carefully
lines: Emergency with siren + blue light: yes

q18428.en: In pedestrian areas vehicles serving disabled people may pass.

explain.short: Vehicles with the disabled badge may enter, so disabled people can reach places.
explain.rule: A pedestrian area (area pedonale) is for pedestrians and bicycles; vehicles enter only as listed exceptions (emergency, disabled, allowed e-vehicles).
explain.trap: 'al servizio di' means 'serving': the vehicle carries a disabled person.

sceneParams.caption: Vehicles for disabled people: allowed
lines: Emergency with siren + blue light: yes

q18429.en: In pedestrian areas police vehicles may pass, with siren and blue flashing light on.

explain.short: Police on an emergency call (siren and blue light on) may go everywhere they need.
explain.rule: A pedestrian area (area pedonale) is for pedestrians and bicycles; vehicles enter only as listed exceptions (emergency, disabled, allowed e-vehicles).
explain.trap: 'in funzione' (switched on) matters: it is an emergency.

sceneParams.caption: Police on emergency may enter
lines: Emergency with siren + blue light: yes

q18430.en: In pedestrian areas fire brigade vehicles may pass, with blue flashing light and siren on.

explain.short: Fire engines on an emergency (blue light and siren on) may enter.
explain.rule: A pedestrian area (area pedonale) is for pedestrians and bicycles; vehicles enter only as listed exceptions (emergency, disabled, allowed e-vehicles).
explain.trap: 'in funzione' (switched on): the emergency devices must be active.

sceneParams.caption: Fire brigade on emergency may enter
lines: Emergency with siren + blue light: yes

q18431.en: In pedestrian areas all motorcycles may pass, provided they give way to pedestrians.

explain.short: Motorcycles may not enter a pedestrian area, even if they give way to people.
explain.rule: A pedestrian area (area pedonale) is for pedestrians and bicycles; vehicles enter only as listed exceptions (emergency, disabled, allowed e-vehicles).
explain.trap: 'tutti' (all) and 'purché' (provided) make a fake condition.

sceneParams.caption: Motorcycles may not enter
lines: Emergency with siren + blue light: yes

q18432.en: In pedestrian areas road tractors may pass, at a speed not over 30 km/h.

explain.short: Road tractors (heavy vehicles that pull trailers) may not enter, at any speed.
explain.rule: A pedestrian area (area pedonale) is for pedestrians and bicycles; vehicles enter only as listed exceptions (emergency, disabled, allowed e-vehicles).
explain.trap: '30 km/h' is an invented condition: speed is not the point.

sceneParams.caption: Tractors may not enter at any speed
lines: Emergency with siren + blue light: yes

q18433.en: In pedestrian areas mopeds may pass only in the daytime.

explain.short: Mopeds may not enter pedestrian areas, day or night.
explain.rule: A pedestrian area (area pedonale) is for pedestrians and bicycles; vehicles enter only as listed exceptions (emergency, disabled, allowed e-vehicles).
explain.trap: 'solo di giorno' (only by day) is invented: they are never allowed.

sceneParams.caption: Mopeds may not enter, day or night
lines: Emergency with siren + blue light: yes

q18434.en: In pedestrian areas all motor vehicles may pass, but with caution.

explain.short: Cars and other motor vehicles are not allowed in; only the listed exceptions are.
explain.rule: A pedestrian area (area pedonale) is for pedestrians and bicycles; vehicles enter only as listed exceptions (emergency, disabled, allowed e-vehicles).
explain.trap: 'tutti' (all) is the trap: only exceptions may enter.

sceneParams.caption: Not all vehicles: only exceptions
lines: Emergency with siren + blue light: yes

q18435.en: In pedestrian areas motor quadricycles may pass, provided they do not exceed 50 km/h.

explain.short: Quadricycles (small four-wheel 'microcars') may not enter; the speed limit is an invented condition.
explain.rule: A pedestrian area (area pedonale) is for pedestrians and bicycles; vehicles enter only as listed exceptions (emergency, disabled, allowed e-vehicles).
explain.trap: 'purché... 50 km/h' is a fake condition.

sceneParams.caption: Quadricycles may not enter
lines: Emergency with siren + blue light: yes

q18436.en: The road can be divided into carriageways.

explain.short: A big road can have two or more carriageways (carreggiate), for example one for each direction.
explain.rule: A road (strada) is the area open to pedestrians, animals and vehicles; it includes carriageways, verges, pavements and cycle lanes.
explain.trap: 'carreggiate' are the parts for vehicles: a road can have several.

sceneParams.caption: A road can have several carriageways

q18437.en: The road can include cycle lanes.

explain.short: Cycle lanes (piste ciclabili) are part of the road, next to the carriageway.
explain.rule: A road (strada) is the area open to pedestrians, animals and vehicles; it includes carriageways, verges, pavements and cycle lanes.
explain.trap: 'comprendere' means 'include'.

sceneParams.caption: Cycle lanes are part of the road

explain.short: Some roads let traffic go in one direction only.
explain.rule: A road (strada) is the area open to pedestrians, animals and vehicles; it includes carriageways, verges, pavements and cycle lanes.
explain.trap: 'senso unico' means one-way.

sceneParams.caption: A road can be one-way

explain.short: Most roads have traffic in both directions.
explain.rule: A road (strada) is the area open to pedestrians, animals and vehicles; it includes carriageways, verges, pavements and cycle lanes.
explain.trap: 'doppio senso' means two-way.

sceneParams.caption: A road can be two-way

q18440.en: The road is open to the traffic of pedestrians, animals and vehicles.

explain.short: This is the legal definition: a road is for everyone, not only cars.
explain.rule: A road (strada) is the area open to pedestrians, animals and vehicles; it includes carriageways, verges, pavements and cycle lanes.
explain.trap: All three users are listed: pedestrians, animals and vehicles.

sceneParams.caption: Road: pedestrians, animals and vehicles

q18441.en: The road does not include the verges.

explain.short: The verge (banchina, the strip at the side of the carriageway) is part of the road.
explain.rule: A road (strada) is the area open to pedestrians, animals and vehicles; it includes carriageways, verges, pavements and cycle lanes.
explain.trap: 'non' makes it false: the road DOES include verges.

sceneParams.caption: The verge IS part of the road

q18442.en: The road is reserved for the traffic of cars and motorcycles only.

explain.short: A road is open to pedestrians, animals and all vehicles, not only cars and motorcycles.
explain.rule: A road (strada) is the area open to pedestrians, animals and vehicles; it includes carriageways, verges, pavements and cycle lanes.
explain.trap: 'soli' (only) is the trap.

sceneParams.caption: Not only cars and motorbikes

q18443.en: The road is normally reserved for the traffic of vehicles and animals only.

explain.short: Pedestrians are missing: a road is also for people on foot.
explain.rule: A road (strada) is the area open to pedestrians, animals and vehicles; it includes carriageways, verges, pavements and cycle lanes.
explain.trap: 'soli' (only) leaves out pedestrians.

sceneParams.caption: Pedestrians use the road too

q18444.en: The road does not include the pavements.

explain.short: The pavement (marciapiede) is part of the road, reserved for pedestrians.
explain.rule: A road (strada) is the area open to pedestrians, animals and vehicles; it includes carriageways, verges, pavements and cycle lanes.
explain.trap: 'non' makes it false: the road DOES include pavements.

sceneParams.caption: The pavement IS part of the road

q18445.en: The road is any asphalted area, bounded at the sides by pedestrian crossings.

explain.short: A road is defined by its use (open to traffic), not by asphalt; crossings do not mark its sides.
explain.rule: A road (strada) is the area open to pedestrians, animals and vehicles; it includes carriageways, verges, pavements and cycle lanes.
explain.trap: 'qualsiasi area asfaltata' sounds plausible but is invented.

sceneParams.caption: Road = area open to traffic, not asphalt

q18446.en: The motorway has no at-grade junctions crossing it.

explain.short: On a motorway nothing crosses at the same level: other roads pass over or under it.
explain.rule: A motorway (autostrada) has separate carriageways, no level junctions, fences and slip lanes; only some vehicles may use it.
explain.trap: 'non ha' (has no) is correct: no level crossroads at all.

sceneParams.caption: No crossroads on a motorway

q18447.en: The motorway has special lanes for vehicles to enter and exit.

explain.short: You join on an acceleration lane and leave on a deceleration lane.
explain.rule: A motorway (autostrada) has separate carriageways, no level junctions, fences and slip lanes; only some vehicles may use it.
explain.trap: 'speciali corsie' are the acceleration and deceleration lanes.

sceneParams.caption: Special lanes to enter and exit

q18448.en: The motorway has independent carriageways or carriageways separated by a central divider.

explain.short: The two directions are kept apart, so there is no head-on traffic.
explain.rule: A motorway (autostrada) has separate carriageways, no level junctions, fences and slip lanes; only some vehicles may use it.
explain.trap: 'spartitraffico' is the central divider between directions.

sceneParams.caption: Directions kept apart by a divider

q18449.en: Motorcycles of at least 150 cc may use the motorway.

explain.short: Motorcycles with an engine of 150 cc or more are allowed on the motorway.
explain.rule: A motorway (autostrada) has separate carriageways, no level junctions, fences and slip lanes; only some vehicles may use it.
explain.trap: 'almeno' (at least) means 150 cc or more.

sceneParams.caption: Motorbikes from 150 cc: allowed

q18450.en: Agricultural machines may not use the motorway.

explain.short: Farm machines are too slow for the motorway, so they are banned.
explain.rule: A motorway (autostrada) has separate carriageways, no level junctions, fences and slip lanes; only some vehicles may use it.
explain.trap: 'non possono' is right: they are banned.

sceneParams.caption: Farm machines: not allowed

q18451.en: Not all types of vehicles may use the motorway.

explain.short: Some vehicles are banned, for example mopeds, bicycles and farm machines.
explain.rule: A motorway (autostrada) has separate carriageways, no level junctions, fences and slip lanes; only some vehicles may use it.
explain.trap: 'non tutti' (not all) is correct: some are excluded.

sceneParams.caption: Some vehicles are banned

q18452.en: Vehicles leave the motorway using deceleration lanes.

explain.short: To exit, you move into the deceleration lane and slow down there, not on the main lanes.
explain.rule: A motorway (autostrada) has separate carriageways, no level junctions, fences and slip lanes; only some vehicles may use it.
explain.trap: 'decelerazione' (slowing down) is for exiting; 'accelerazione' is for entering.

sceneParams.caption: Exit via the deceleration lane

q18453.en: The motorway must be fenced at the sides.

explain.short: A fence keeps people and animals off the motorway.
explain.rule: A motorway (autostrada) has separate carriageways, no level junctions, fences and slip lanes; only some vehicles may use it.
explain.trap: 'deve' (must): the fence is required.

sceneParams.caption: Motorways are fenced

explain.short: Trucks, buses and big motorcycles also use the motorway.
explain.rule: A motorway (autostrada) has separate carriageways, no level junctions, fences and slip lanes; only some vehicles may use it.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) is the trap.

sceneParams.caption: Not only cars: trucks, buses, big bikes

q18455.en: All types of motorcycles may use motorways.

explain.short: Small motorcycles are not allowed: in the quiz the minimum is 150 cc.
explain.rule: A motorway (autostrada) has separate carriageways, no level junctions, fences and slip lanes; only some vehicles may use it.
explain.trap: 'tutti' (all) is the trap.

sceneParams.caption: Not all motorbikes: minimum engine size

q18456.en: The motorway can include cycle lanes.

explain.short: Bicycles are banned from motorways, so there are no cycle lanes.
explain.rule: A motorway (autostrada) has separate carriageways, no level junctions, fences and slip lanes; only some vehicles may use it.
explain.trap: 'piste ciclabili' never belong to a motorway.

sceneParams.caption: No cycle lanes on motorways

q18457.en: Mopeds and motorcycles up to 125 cc may use motorways.

explain.short: Mopeds are never allowed on motorways, and in the quiz motorcycles need at least 150 cc.
explain.rule: A motorway (autostrada) has separate carriageways, no level junctions, fences and slip lanes; only some vehicles may use it.
explain.trap: 'ciclomotori' (mopeds) alone already makes it wrong.

sceneParams.caption: Mopeds never; small motorbikes no

q18457.reviewNote: Legge 177/2024 may allow motorcycles from 120 cc ridden by adults on motorways; check the 125 cc part.

q18458.en: Only motor vehicles (autoveicoli) may use motorways.

explain.short: Big motorcycles (motoveicoli, not autoveicoli) are also allowed, so 'only autoveicoli' is wrong.
explain.rule: A motorway (autostrada) has separate carriageways, no level junctions, fences and slip lanes; only some vehicles may use it.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) is the trap: motorcycles are not autoveicoli.

sceneParams.caption: Big motorbikes are allowed too

q18459.en: All motorcycles and mopeds may use motorways.

explain.short: Mopeds are banned and small motorcycles are banned too.
explain.rule: A motorway (autostrada) has separate carriageways, no level junctions, fences and slip lanes; only some vehicles may use it.
explain.trap: 'tutti' (all) plus 'ciclomotori' make it wrong twice.

sceneParams.caption: No mopeds, no small motorbikes

explain.short: A carriageway can carry traffic in one direction only, for example on a dual road.
explain.rule: The carriageway (carreggiata) is the part of the road for moving vehicles; it can have lanes and one or two directions.
explain.trap: 'senso unico' means one-way; 'può' means it is possible.

sceneParams.caption: A carriageway can be one-way

explain.short: Many carriageways carry traffic in both directions.
explain.rule: The carriageway (carreggiata) is the part of the road for moving vehicles; it can have lanes and one or two directions.
explain.trap: 'doppio senso' means two-way.

sceneParams.caption: A carriageway can be two-way

q18462.en: The carriageway can be divided into lanes.

explain.short: Lines can split the carriageway into lanes (corsie), each wide enough for one line of vehicles.
explain.rule: The carriageway (carreggiata) is the part of the road for moving vehicles; it can have lanes and one or two directions.
explain.trap: 'corsie' (lanes) are smaller parts of the 'carreggiata'.

sceneParams.caption: Carriageway split into lanes

q18463.en: The carriageway does not include cycle lanes.

explain.short: Cycle lanes are part of the ROAD, but outside the carriageway.
explain.rule: The carriageway (carreggiata) is the part of the road for moving vehicles; it can have lanes and one or two directions.
explain.trap: Do not confuse 'strada' (includes cycle lanes) with 'carreggiata' (does not).

sceneParams.caption: Cycle lanes are outside the carriageway

q18464.en: The carriageway does not include pavements.

explain.short: Pavements are for pedestrians, outside the carriageway.
explain.rule: The carriageway (carreggiata) is the part of the road for moving vehicles; it can have lanes and one or two directions.
explain.trap: Here 'non comprende' is right: pavements are separate.

sceneParams.caption: Pavements are outside the carriageway

q18465.en: The carriageway is the part of the road normally intended for vehicle traffic.

explain.short: This is the definition of carriageway: where vehicles normally drive.
explain.rule: The carriageway (carreggiata) is the part of the road for moving vehicles; it can have lanes and one or two directions.
explain.trap: 'parte della strada' (part of the road): the carriageway is inside the road.

sceneParams.caption: Carriageway = where vehicles drive

q18466.en: The carriageway is intended only for the traffic of animal-drawn carts.

explain.short: The carriageway is for all vehicles, not only for carts pulled by animals.
explain.rule: The carriageway (carreggiata) is the part of the road for moving vehicles; it can have lanes and one or two directions.
explain.trap: 'carreggiata' sounds like 'carro' (cart), and 'soltanto' (only) is the trap.

sceneParams.caption: For all vehicles, not only carts

q18467.en: The carriageway is intended for emergency stops.

explain.short: The carriageway is for moving traffic. Emergency stops go on the emergency lane or verge.
explain.rule: The carriageway (carreggiata) is the part of the road for moving vehicles; it can have lanes and one or two directions.
explain.trap: 'sosta di emergenza' belongs to the emergency lane, not the carriageway.

sceneParams.caption: Emergency stops: emergency lane, not here

q18468.en: The carriageway is intended for truck parking.

explain.short: The carriageway is for moving traffic, not for parking trucks.
explain.rule: The carriageway (carreggiata) is the part of the road for moving vehicles; it can have lanes and one or two directions.
explain.trap: 'sosta' (parking) is the wrong use.

sceneParams.caption: For moving traffic, not truck parking

q18469.en: The carriageway is the track left by vehicle wheels on snowy roads.

explain.short: The carriageway is a fixed part of the road, not wheel marks in the snow.
explain.rule: The carriageway (carreggiata) is the part of the road for moving vehicles; it can have lanes and one or two directions.
explain.trap: 'traccia' (track) plays on 'carreggiata' (also 'wheel rut' in common speech).

sceneParams.caption: A road part, not wheel tracks in snow

explain.short: Lay-bys (piazzole di sosta) are outside the carriageway, so you can stop there without blocking traffic.
explain.rule: The carriageway (carreggiata) is the part of the road for moving vehicles; it can have lanes and one or two directions.
explain.trap: 'piazzole di sosta' are for stopping, so they are outside the carriageway.

sceneParams.caption: Lay-bys are outside the carriageway
